plan.english: It was growing dark. The night grew cold. The shepherd's wife lay in the house and her husband was awake. Then the dawn grew bright and the sky was red, and a son came forth. He cried out. Then the father saw him and his own heart grew joyful. Then the father showed him the sun, and set a famous name on him, and said: "May you live many years; may your name not die; may imperishable fame be yours!" The mother heard him and said: "Dear is he to us; may he grow up, and may he be strong!"

title: A Father Greets His Daughter at the Fire

plan.english: Snow lay on the field. The father sat by the fire, grasping his daughter, and said: "A daughter is born to me in the winter. Your mother toiled in the night. Fire, hear me, you who guard us! Now I set a famous name for my daughter. Daughter, may you grow up in my household, and may you be dear to your husband; may there be much wool for you; may the frost not seize you; may the fire warm you; may sons be born to you, and may daughters be born to you." So he spoke, and the fire burned.

title: A Prayer to Sky and Earth for the Newborn

plan.english: Dear Father Sky, hear us! Dear Mother Earth, protect this offspring! Giver of good things, give him a lifetime! Dawn, daughter of Sky, grow bright for him! Swift wheel of the sun, be bright for him! May he grow up in our household, and may he be strong! May dear swift horses be his! May his sheep be many! May men hear his good name! May he become an old man, and then may he die!

The maternal grandfather arrived at the house and saw his own grandson. Then he said to the father: "Which name have you set on him?" He answered: "I set on him the name of my father." "Was he famous?" "He was famous; great fame was his, and he slew the serpent." "Where did he slay it?" "He slew it by the river." Then the grandfather said: "May he be famous; may he grow strong, and may men listen to his name." He gave a ram to the grandson, and a woman brought wine, and the two sat down and drank mead.

An old man was sitting. The snow was melting, and the river was filling. His daughter-in-law came to him and said: "Father-in-law, a son is born to me." The old man looked at him, and he was glad and said: "I am old, and I shall die; my name shall not die. I set my name on my grandson; he shall carry it forward. Mortals die; a famous name lives."

title: A Charm to Guard the Newborn

plan.english: Wolf, do not come, do not seize the offspring! And now, dog, guard him; dog, lie down by him! If the wolf comes, then may the dog kill him! Wolf, flee; now, Fire, burn in the night! Dawn, drive the night away! May the old wolf not see him! And now, Earth, hold him up! Beasts, go away from him! And now, Sun, warm him!

When a son is born to a man, his friends come to his household carrying gifts. The shepherd leads a ram; the cook cooks it for the guests; the woman brings honey; the smith makes a gift; the carpenter builds a yoke for him; the master gives them mead, and they drink, and they eat. Whoever brings a gift, to him the master gives a gift. Friends are many, and the offspring grows.

What does the man carry? It is not on his shoulder. His father set it on him at birth. Men say it. The man listens to it. No one eats it, no one drinks it. Fire does not burn it, water does not carry it away. When the man lies in the earth, it lives. What is it? It is the name.

title: The Suitors Come to the House

plan.english: The son of a man came to love the daughter of the master. He spoke to his own father. Then the father said to his own brother: "Let us go to the master, and let us seek his daughter for my son." Then the two went, and led ten cattle before them. They arrived, and the master saw them and said: "Sit down, guests." They sat down, and he set mead before them. Then the guest said: "We have come; we seek your daughter. The bride-price of your daughter is ten cattle." The master listened, and said: "I am listening to you. Drink the wine, and I shall speak with my wife."

The master and the man sat, and the master said: "Which bride-price do you give for my daughter?" "I give ten cattle and ten sheep." "My daughter is good and dear; give many sheep!" "And I give two swift horses. Great is my gift." "Where are the horses?" "They stand by the river." Then the master said: "Your gift is great, and I shall give my daughter to your son. Lead them into my field." "So be it. He shall lead her to his house." Then the master looked at them, and his heart grew joyful.

If a man gives the bride-price of a daughter and her father takes it and does not give the daughter, let him give the bride-price back twice. If a woman goes away from her husband to another man, let her father give the bride-price back to the husband. If a man leads a woman into his household and gives no bride-price, let him give ten sheep to her father. If a man breaks the pledge, let him give ten cattle to the other. Whoever strikes the woman of another, let him give a ram to her husband. Whoever takes a gift and gives nothing, that man is of ill fame. That is what is established.

The daughter came to her father, and he said to her: "A man has come to us; he seeks you. Will you go to him?" The daughter said: "I shall go, and I am afraid of the dwelling of strangers." Then the mother said to her: "Do not tremble! When I came to this household, I became afraid. I have seen the man, and he is good. His dwelling is bright; and his horses are swift." Then the daughter stood up and went to her mother.

Dawn grew bright. The master's daughter came forth, and her mother cried out, and clothed her in a garment of wool. The garment was red. The men yoked the cattle to the wagon. The wagon was the work of the carpenter, and the yoke was the work of the smith. Her husband lifted her up onto it, and her brother followed her. The wheel of the sun was bright. The daughter looked back, and her heart trembled. They passed the stone and the tree. At night they arrived at the house of her father-in-law. The father-in-law stood in front and said: "Enter, daughter."

title: A Father's Words at the Wagon

plan.english: The father stood before the wagon and spoke to his daughter: "Daughter, you go from my house to the dwelling of your husband. Listen to your father-in-law, and guard his fire. Do not deceive your husband; be dear to his brother. Take the wool, the garment, and the ram. Remember your mother. Nourish your offspring. May the gods make your path straight. If distress comes upon you, come to us. Our dwelling stands for you. Go, daughter!"

Now enter your own dwelling, mistress! Mistress, be good to your father-in-law! Be dear to your husband's brother! And may the fire indeed be bright for you! May your two horses be swift! And now may there be much butter for you! Perkwunos, pass by this dwelling! May your seed indeed be many! May you nourish ten dear sons! May you two live many years! And may you two indeed grow old together! And now, Sun, look upon you together! And Dawn, daughter of Sky, shine for you! Father Sky, hear our word! And now give them good things!

title: The Pledge of the Two Fathers

plan.english: The man and the master sat down. The master said: "I give you my daughter. Give me your pledge." The two gave their pledges. Then the man said: "The sky hears, and Mother Earth hears. The sun has seen it, and the river knows it. Whoever breaks this pledge, may his cattle vanish, may his name die!" Then the two drank wine, and night came.

title: The New Wife at the Fire

plan.english: The fire was burning, the smoke went up, and the wife sat down by it. Her father-in-law looked at her, and she trembled. Then the brother of her husband brought water and set it before her. Then the sister of her husband gave her a garment, and she clothed herself in the garment. The sister showed her the wool. Then the father-in-law said: "Daughter, you are a daughter to us. Eat the honey and the butter, and drink the mead; our fire is yours." She ate, she drank, and her heart grew warm. The dog lay down by her.

title: The Quarrel of the Two Wives

plan.english: Two brothers dwelt together. The two wives drew water from the river. Their husbands were at work; the sun was burning. The wife of one brother spoke to the wife of the other: "You have deceived me." She said: "I did not deceive you." Then the words ran to the husbands. One brother struck the other, and blood came forth. The two women cried out, and the father-in-law heard. He came, and stood between the two. "Let go! What have you done?" Distress filled the household. The two stood, and looked down.

A brother is a stronghold for a brother. A deceiving tongue splits brothers. The tongue is a serpent. The word of an old man is a path. The heart of a mother is a fire. A good father-in-law is a fire in winter. A good daughter-in-law is honey. A brother-in-law of ill fame is a worm in the apple. She who deceives her husband is a wolf in the dwelling. For the deceiver there is honey on the tongue, and a serpent in the heart. A wolf does not become a dog. Two brothers draw the wagon under the yoke. Where brothers sit together, there the fire burns. This is the old word.

At night the woman came to her husband and said: "Hear me. Your brother has spoken to me. He said: 'You are a stranger in our house. You eat our honey and our butter.' I am not a stranger; I am your wife." He listened to her, and said: "Did he say this?" "He said it." "I shall go to my brother, and I shall speak to him. You are not a stranger in this household; you are dear to me." Then he rose, and went to him. He found him with the horses, and spoke to him.

title: The Judgment of the Old Father

plan.english: The two brothers stood before the father. He listened to the two, and then he said: "Whoever struck his own brother, let that man give a ram to the other. And she who deceived, let her bring water to the woman of the other." The two heard his word. That man led a ram to him, and she brought water. Then the old man said: "Sit down, and drink the wine. The blood of a brother is not water." The two sat down, and drank.

title: The Widow and Her Husband's Brother

plan.english: In winter the husband drove the flock to the field. The snow came, and he did not come back. His wife sat by the fire and looked at the path. The wolves cried out in the night. At dawn she saw him; the snow lay on him; the frost seized him; he was dead. She became a widow and cried out. The brother of her husband came. He said: "Woman, do not cry out. I shall nourish your offspring, and I shall guard your field." Then the widow said: "You are good, and I shall dwell in your household." So the widow dwelt in his household.

If a man strikes his father, let him go out. If a man takes the field of a brother, let him give it back and a ram. Whoever deceives his brother-in-law, let no one give him a gift. If a daughter-in-law strikes her father-in-law, let her go back to her own dwelling. If a father-in-law drives away a good daughter-in-law, let him give her ten sheep. If a man kills his brother, let him not dwell in the village. If a man steals the sheep of his brother-in-law, let him give them back twice.

The father spoke to the brothers: "Sit together, and let the two women sit down. The words that you spoke, let the river carry them away. I am old, and I shall die; afterwards wolves will come to the flock; you two shall guard the flock together." Then the two sat down, and the two women sat with them. He saw them, and the fire was bright, and his heart grew warm.

title: The Old Man Divides His Flock

plan.english: The father sat down. Three brothers stood before him. He spoke to them: "I am old, and death is coming to me. Hear me. To the one who ploughs I give the field; to the one who guards the sheep I give the cattle; to the one who drives the horses I give the wagon. Do not strike your brothers, and may your name be good among men." They heard his word. Then he drank mead, and lay down.

The old man sat in the sun and spoke: "I was swift, I ploughed, I drove the flock to the river, I went over the sea in a boat, I killed the wolf. Now I am old, and I am blind. I sit by the fire. My heart is bright, and great fame is mine. May my name live."

The father lay down, and the three sat by him. One son said: "To whom do you give the house?" The old man answered: "I give it to him who nourishes me." Another said: "I bring you water." "I milk the cows for you." The old man saw their work, and pointed out the middle one. The middle one said: "I did not nourish you for the house." "The house is yours."

Whoever nourishes an old father, to him shall belong the old man's house. And whoever leaves an old father, let him have nothing of the flock. If a man has no son, the descendant of his daughter shall take the field. If he has no descendant, his brother shall take it. Let the widow guard the field for the offspring. No one shall take it.

Their father was dead. The three brothers sat down. The one who drove the horses said: "The horses are mine." The one who ploughs said: "Give me two horses." "I shall not give them." Then one brother struck the other, and the other struck him. They fled, and they ran to the river. The river carried a horse away. Then they saw it in the water, and became afraid. The one who guards the sheep cried out: "What are you doing?"

At night the three brothers sat down. The middle one spoke: "Our father is dead. Shall we split the cattle, or shall we keep them together?" The one who ploughs said: "The sheep that go apart, the wolf kills them." The one who guards the sheep said: "Let us keep the flock together, and let us not split the field, and let us dwell in our household." The middle one said: "So be it." Then they gave libated mead to the dead man.

title: The Great Bull and the Old Bull

plan.english: A great bull led the flock, and an old bull went with him. The great bull said to him: "You are old. Go away from us." He went away. The sun was burning, and the river dried up. The flock was thirsty. The great bull did not find water. The other stood by the stone. He said: "I know the water. It is under the stone." He led them to it, and they drank, and they were sated. The great bull has force; the old bull knows the path.

The widow came before the king. The queen was sitting beside the king. The widow said: "King, I am a widow, and my husband is dead. The brothers of my husband are seizing my field. Protect me and my offspring!" The king looked at the widow, and said to them: "To whom does it belong?" They said: "It is ours." The king said: "It is for the offspring of the widow. Give it back, and give ten sheep to the widow." They heard the king, and gave it back.

The old man lay, and his breath was leaving him. His offspring stood around him. He said: "Listen to me. I am thirsty; bring me water. I go to the fathers. Keep the flock together, and do not strike your brother. Give me libated mead, cover me with earth, and set up a stone. Remember my name." Then he did not speak again, and they cried out.

Husband, you are indeed gone away! Who will guard the sheep, who will plough? Now I am a widow, and my heart has grown cold! The fire burns, but you do not sit by it. I look at your place; where indeed are you? I look at the road, come back, dear husband! And your offspring cry out. The dog looks for you; I cooked for you, you do not eat! And now the earth covers you.

Father, you are leaving us, we are your offspring! And now who indeed will lead us forward? Who will sit in your place? Your words are indeed in our ears. And your name is on our tongue. And now dawn grows bright, and you do not wake. And you indeed were great among men. Imperishable fame is yours. Now we set up a stone above you. Lie in the earth, we shall keep your word.

At dawn the brothers carried the dead man out of the dwelling. They clothed him in a garment. The procession followed him. They laid him on the wood, and brought fire. The fire burned him, and the smoke went up to the sky. His wife cried out, and the dog cried out. Then they covered him with earth. They set up a stone above him, and gave libated mead to the dead man. The sun sank. Then night came, and the dog lay down by the stone.

The three brothers stood at the stone. The middle one said: "Father Sky, listen to us. Earth, listen to us. We give you an oath. We shall keep the cattle together; we shall not split the flock. Let no one of us strike his brother. Whoever breaks this oath, may the sky strike him, and may the earth not carry him."

The warrior lay down and spoke to his sons: "I was a warrior. I slew the serpent, and I struck down the enemies of the king. I drove the chariot of the king. Great fame is mine. Now death is coming to me, and I am not afraid. Mortals die; the gods do not die. If the name of a man lives, his fame is imperishable. Let your fame be great." Then his breath left him.

The sister sat by the stone. Her brother arrived, and she said to him: "Our father is dead. Who guards the cattle now?" He said: "I guard them. Who nourishes our mother?" "I nourish her." Then he said: "Sister, what will you do?" She said: "I shall keep the fire, and I shall remember his words." Then the dog came, and lay down between them.

title: A Prayer for the Dead Father

plan.english: Father, go by the path, and go by the path of the fathers! Cross the river in the boat, may the boat carry him! Dawn, daughter of Sky, grow bright for him! Now, Sun, look upon him, Mother Earth, receive him! May he sit with the fathers, and may he drink the libated mead! And may his name not die! May his fame be imperishable, and we remember him.
